title: Octave Web's sign-in: page scripts can't read it, other sites can't use it
description: Serves "Joining and signing in are easy and safe."; "Access is enforced everywhere.". D-111; #301 (Octave's web session), whose need stands and whose shapes are jellyscale's to decide.
acceptanceCriteria: A browser signs in (by password, and by single sign-on through JS-039) and holds no credential its page's scripts can read.

A request from another site, or from another service on the same host name, is refused even when the browser sends the sign-in with it; the protection does not rest on the browser's cookie rules alone, shown with forged requests from another port on the same name.
Signing out ends it at once; it ends after stated idle and absolute times; a password change ends the account's other web sign-ins; a viewer sees and ends their own (JS-042).
Behind a proxy that ends HTTPS, it is still marked secure, from the configured external address.
No sign-in answer is kept by a cache, and no secret of it is stored unhashed or appears in a log or an error body.
The Octave Web pages the server serves carry response headers that limit what scripts and framing can do, and docs/running.md says what a proxy in front must keep.
DOMAINS invariant 63 is reworded as D-111 records; the header-token API is unchanged.
Every capability it adds is in the published contract (JS-183) and passes its conformance check.

The web sign-in is accepted on picture routes, whose answers are marked private so no shared cache keeps them, and never on any other media request (a stream, a segment, a subtitle, a font) or a media link.
